title: Mocking Dependencies with unittest.mock
learningObjectives: Explain Mock, patch, return_value, side_effect and call assertions.
Select a suitable testing or code-quality technique for PY21.11.
Interpret test, diagnostic and quality-tool output correctly.
Identify limitations and risks when applying PY21.11.
Apply PY21.11 concepts in a maintainable Python workflow.

understand.concept: Mocking replaces or simulates a dependency during a test so the code under test can be checked without relying on a real external service or slow resource. unittest.mock is part of the standard library. Mock objects can return configured values, raise exceptions with side_effect and record how they were called. Patch the name where the code under test looks it up.
understand.whyItMatters: Mocking isolates a unit from external systems and makes tests faster and more predictable when used at the correct boundary.
understand.analogy: A mock is a practice partner that imitates a real service so a function can be tested without contacting the actual service.
understand.analogyLimit: Over-mocking can make tests verify implementation details rather than meaningful behaviour; mocks do not prove that the real integration works.
understand.summary: Mocking Dependencies with unittest.mock develops reliable testing and code-quality skills for Python projects.

explain.narrative:
## Isolate dependencies with mocks
Use `unittest.mock.Mock` to create a mock object and configure `return_value` for a predictable response. `side_effect` can provide a sequence of values or raise an exception. Use `assert_called_once_with()` and `call_count` to inspect interactions.

The `patch()` helper temporarily replaces a name during a test. Patch the symbol in the namespace where the code under test uses it, not automatically where it was originally defined. Keep at least some integration tests that exercise the real boundary.

examples.title: Configure a mock return value
examples.code:
from unittest.mock import Mock
service = Mock()
service.fetch_status.return_value = 'ready'
print(service.fetch_status())
examples.explanation: return_value configures the value returned by a mock method.

examples.title: Inspect a mock call
examples.code:
from unittest.mock import Mock
sender = Mock()
sender.send('hello')
print(sender.send.call_count)
print(sender.send.call_args.args[0])
examples.explanation: Mock records calls and their arguments.

examples.title: Assert a call with arguments
examples.code:
from unittest.mock import Mock
worker = Mock()
worker.process('job-7')
worker.process.assert_called_once_with('job-7')
print('verified')
examples.explanation: assert_called_once_with checks both call count and argument values.

examples.title: Simulate a dependency exception
examples.explanation: side_effect can raise an exception to simulate a failing dependency.

examples.title: Return a sequence of responses
examples.code:
from unittest.mock import Mock
clock = Mock(side_effect=[10, 20, 30])
print(clock(), clock(), clock())
examples.explanation: An iterable side_effect supplies successive values for successive calls.

practise.guidedTask: Write a function that calls a small service object. Replace that service with Mock, configure its return value and assert it was called with the expected arguments.
practise.independentTask: Plan mock-based tests for a function that sends a notification. Identify what to mock, what behaviour to assert and which real integration test is still required.
hints: Use unittest.mock.Mock for a mock object.
Set return_value for a predictable response.
Use side_effect to simulate an exception.
Patch the name where the tested code looks it up.
practise.challenge: Design a test suite for a payment-status adapter using mocks for network boundaries and a separate integration test for the adapter contract; never use real payment credentials.
